title: Clicking a cut, keying a value and undoing it answer inside 50 ms
goal: On a video, a click on a cut still keeps the app busy for 60 to 70 ms, the first value picked to animate for 45 to 63 ms, and Undo of it for about 70 ms, measured now exactly as a person gets them. Bring all three under the 50 ms the video goals ask for; most of the cost is the right hand panel taking down or redrawing sections a person cannot see.
notes:
Carried from a-first-clip-pick-and-a-cut-click-answer-inside (2026-10-07), whose log has the measurements. The four timed walks now say setup timedWithoutMarkers, so their numbers are the dev app's, not the probe's (probe markers were ~25 ms of every click). Numbers on 2026-10-07 without markers: cut 54-76 (median ~68), first clip pick 33-50 (median ~48), deselect ~58, Position pick 40-53 in animate-pick-cost, 57 in keyframe-anything, 63 in an-editing-session; undo median 71.

Attribution for the cut (A/B interleaved, temp switches, all reverted): panel switched off entirely -> cut 24, first pick 20, so the panel is ~44 ms of a cut. Blanking the nine sections a cut drops (keys,speed,color,effects,sound,fades,gain,soundEffects,captions) -> 42; blanking the three that stay (editPoint,transition,transitions) -> 66, so it is the TEARDOWN of the leaving sections. One at a time: captions -11 ms (710pt form, below the fold), keys/speed/color/gain/effects/sound/fades 1-3 ms each. In the cut pass ~23% is accessibility (AX graph update 8%, focus walk 8%, needsUpdate 7%), ~12% AppKit view removal/dealloc, ~9% PlatformViewChild updates. A transition picker popover opens a pass later (fine); the previous popover's window is released inside the cut pass (~1.5 ms).

Tried and measured, NOT shipped: (1) sections leaving a pass later, kept built and drawn as nothing (zero-height frame, out-of-sight placement, or visible at the end): every variant was slower (64-86 vs 46-60 interleaved) because the kept sections re-render for the new selection, and a zero-height frame re-lays out their forms. (2) tutorial anchors hung only while a guide runs: -2 to -3 ms. (3) a dropdown face drawn without its nested NSHostingView: profile says ~2 ms of nine dropdowns' teardown. Structural lever left: build only the panel sections near the viewport (a clip's twelve sections, ~600pt visible of ~1800pt; the dropped ones below the fold are ~18 ms of the cut), which needs the walk harness to scroll-search for controls in unbuilt sections. Noise between rounds is 15-20 ms; only interleaved runs compare (an xctrace SwiftUI recording in the background inflated one round).
acceptance: The first value picked from Animate a property (Position on a typed title) holds under 50 ms in three runs each of keyframe-anything-walk and an-editing-session-walk
Undoing that pick holds under 50 ms in Scripts/playtest/perf/animate-pick-cost-walk.json (median of twelve)
The panel shows the cut after a cut click and the clip after a piece click, in the click's own frame, and keyframe-anything-walk keeps its build-count claims

log.note: Reproduced 2026-10-07 (clip-click-cost-walk, no flags): cut 54-83 median ~68, first pick 48-53. A/B with temp switches: placeholders for EVERY below-fold section was SLOWER (cut median 81: the cut then builds Edit point, Transition and Transitions in its frame); placeholders only for the below-fold sections a cut drops (Fades, Gain, Audio Effects, Captions) saved ~12 ms (67 -> 54).

Shipped db5108a9: PanelBodyReach (core, 16 tests) + flag next-panel-builds-what-you-see (on in Next, video documents only, off while a guide runs). A section arriving >120pt below the panel's bottom waits as a same-height space and builds when scrolled near, one per pass; a built section stays built wherever a pick carries it (so a cut keeps Edit point/Transitions built). Captions' late rows (PanelRowsArrival) are let go after 0.5s far out of sight. Harness: a lookup that misses while something waits turns on PanelBuildsEverything for the rest of the walk (in patiently, plus one retry of a failed step).

Measured, interleaved vs switch off, 3 rounds: cut 70 -> 57 ms median (about a third of cuts at or under 50 with it on), first clip pick 49 -> 40 (all under 50), deselect 55 -> 51. Unchanged: Position pick 54 keyframe-anything, 63 an-editing-session, 44-52 animate-pick-cost; undo median 69. Green: clip-click-cost, keyframe-anything (build counts held), an-editing-session, plus 17 caption/section/transition walks; a scroll check shows Gain, Audio Effects and Captions filled in after a scroll; Scripts/test.sh 11717 pass.

Time Profiler of the cut pass after the change (12 cuts): diffuse. ~61% is SwiftUI's update+layout of the window, ~9% AppGraph/EditorCommands re-evaluating the menu bar on the selection change (~3 ms a cut; canAddZoom and canSuggestZooms do a trial edit on a copy of the document), ~2.5 ms AppKitPopUpAdaptor updating a header menu's items (accessibility per item), 6.5% AccessibilityViewGraph.needsUpdate, 8% autorelease pool dealloc. Left rough here, not filed (no person notices any one of them): the next pass at the 50 ms bar starts with the menu bar commands and the header menus.

Blocked on a decision for what is left of keying and undo: keying Position grows the timeline a lane and the picture refits 74% -> 71% (undo back to 74%), read off animate-pick-cost-walk's displayZoom. Keeping the timeline's height is a visible change, so it is a card. No audit: nothing a person sees changed except speed (a section scrolled into view fills in; the probe pictures show it already filled).

Partly met, rest waits on a card. Shipped db5108a9 (pushed): on a video the panel builds only the sections near view. Cut 70 -> 57 ms, first clip pick 49 -> 40 (under 50), deselect 55 -> 51; walks green, 11717 tests pass. Keying Position and its undo are unchanged (~50-63, ~69): the largest piece left is the timeline growing a lane and the picture refitting 74% -> 71%, which is a visible change, so it is a decision card.

Manager pass 2026-10-07: the 12:36 an-editing-session-walk shows a deferred hold after keying as well as the press itself: Animate a property click, longest 288 ms from 408 ms in; Position pick, 311 ms from 485 ms in. Undo of a cut, a ripple delete and a drop hold 166-222 ms from ~240 ms in (filed as undo-and-redo-on-a-video-answer-at-once). One deferred job may explain both.

The deferred holds the manager saw here (Animate a property 288ms from 408ms in, Position 311ms from 485ms in) were the walk's own markers going back up, not the app: fixed in a226b321. an-editing-session-walk now reads Animate a property 35.8ms, Position 59.5ms, with the re-hang (298ms, 324ms) named and left out. Also carried in from undo-and-redo-on-a-video-answer-at-once: Undo/Redo of a cut, ripple delete and clip drop are 46-77ms (median ~62) in Scripts/playtest/undo-redo-cost-walk.json, same editor-wide cost as the cut click; ~20% of each is SwiftUI accessibility upkeep, app code ~10ms.
